newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas ends down, AGAs drive ACCESS higher.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas ends down, AGAs drive ACCESS higher.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures, pressured by milder East Coast and Midwest weather forecasts, mostly ended lower Wednesday in sluggish trade, then moved up on ACCESS after bullish weekly inventory data.

August slipped 4.3 cents to close at $2.067 per million British thermal units, then jumped to $2.095 in after-hours trade on the AGA stock report. Sept settled 4.3 cents lower at $2.07. Most other deferreds ended down by 0.1 to 3.8 cents.
"The (AGA) number was on the low end of expectations, but I'm not sure it's that constructive. It was a hot week and this week we should build a lot more," said an eastern trader.

AGA said Wednesday that U.S. gas stocks rose last week by 76 bcf, well-below average estimates in the 85-95 bcf range. Overall stocks are still 216 bcf, or 16 percent, over year-ago levels. Eastern storage gained 56 bcf and was 11 percent above last year, while producing region inventories remained 52 percent over 1996 levels. Western stocks continued to lag year-ago levels by nine percent.

Despite the moderately bullish inventory report, traders said cooler weather expected in the East and Midwest later this week and next should temper any buying spree. Heat was expected to continue in Texas and the Southwest next week.

Chart traders said August's dip Tuesday below trendline support set the stage for weakness Wednesday. Next support was seen at $2.055, the spot continuation low on June 12, with further buying likely at $2. Resistance remained at $2.15 and then along the down trendline at $2.27. Further selling was likely at the recent $2.36 high and then at the $2.415 contract high.

In the cash Wednesday, Gulf Coast prices slipped a few cents to about the $2.10 level. Midcon pipes were down slightly in the $2.02-2.03 area. New York city gate gas was quoted three to four cents lower in the high-$2.30s.
The NYMEX Henry Hub 12-month strip tumbled three cents to $2.161. NYMEX said 28,730 contracts traded, up from Tuesday's revised tally of 17,602.
NYMEX natgas trade will close at 1300 EDT Thursday ahead of the Independence Day holiday Friday.

On the KCBT, August finished 3.2 cents lower at $1.95, while deferreds ended down by two to 5.5 cents. The East/West spread narrowed by 1.1 cents to 11.7 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 83 lots traded, down from Tuesday's total of 167.
